newsitem.title: UK: Firmer Wall Stret drags European bourses off floor.
newsitem.headline: Firmer Wall Stret drags European bourses off floor.

text.p: European stock markets crawled off their lows on Wednesday after Wall Street bounced back modestly from Tuesday's gyrations.
Frayed nerves caused by the Dow Jones average's 100 point surge then plunge overnight earlier sent European investors into retreat.
But the Dow, taking its lead from bonds after favourable durable goods data, racked up early gains and helped to steady European bourses.
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar retreated from fresh highs overnight. It was trading off its lows by mid-afternoon with traders saying the upward trend appeared intact.
By 1500 GMT the dollar was quoted at 1.6380 marks and 121.57 yen, well off its near four-year high of 122.78 yen and 1.6555 marks.
The surprise December decline in orders for U.S. manufactured goods was seen supporting the theory that the American economy was growing moderately.
"This report doesn't change the very moderate uptrend in orders and in fact underscores the softness in the economy." William Griggs, managing director of Griggs & Santow Inc in New York, said.
Despite the early rise on Wall Street, George Pirrone of Dreyfus Corp in New York warned more volatility could be laying in wait.
"I wouldn't count out another little dance to the downside. The long bond yield is getting dangerously close to that seven percent mark, and that puts the lid on any major rallies."
London's blue chip FTSE 100 share index limped off its lows but investors remained wary of what might still happen on Wall Street following Tuesday's see-saw session.
By 1500 GMT the FTSE was 35 points weaker at 4,202 after earlier sliding below 4,200.

"Data on both sides of the Atlantic has been fairly bullish recently," one London trader said. "But although people's heads tell them this is a buying opportunity, their hearts tell them they don't want to be in the market."

Next week sees crucial interest rate meetings in both the U.S. and Britain. The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting is due on Tuesday and Wednesday with Britain's monthly monetary meeting on Wednesday.
"Volatility is rising. I look for equities and bonds to remain weak," said Kirit Shah, strategist at Sanwa International.
French shares recovered some of their lost ground, overcoming some of their earlier jitters with the firmer start on Wall Street.
The CAC-40 index lost 1.5 percent as the market reacted to the U.S. orders data but by 1500 GMT was showing a loss of 21 points, or 0.87 percent, at 2,461.
Wall Street's overnight turnaround shocked the German share market and left it trapped in a narrow range throughout a markedly cautious floor session.

The 30-share DAX index, catching up with a surge in late electronic dealing on Tuesday, ended 9.87 points higher. However, the IBIS DAX, which tracks post-bourse dealings, was down some 32 points from Tuesday's closing level.

Chemical shares, which were overlooked in a recent switch to exporters, were the strongest blue chip sector. BASF AG advanced 80 pfennigs to 59.90 marks in heavy trade while Bayer AG rose 75 pfennigs to 62.30 marks.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6385 marks and 121.57 yen compared with late Tuesday's European level of 1.6496 marks and 121.31 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading shares was down 35.2 points, or 0.83 percent, at 4,202.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 21.66 points, or 0.87 percent, at 2,461.1.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 9.87 points, or 0.33 percent, at 2,999.2. In later screen trade, the IBIS DAX was down 32.8 points at 2,995.47.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed slightly firmer at $351.10 against $350.15 in the morning and $353.70 on Tuesday afternoon. Silver was seven cents easier at $4.91.
